description: BenchKeeper sets up Claude Code and Codex with one rules file and four skills. It is for developers who use Claude Code or Codex and want the same rules, skills and devcontainer setup in every repository. The setup skills install and check rules, skills and tools, per machine and per repository: CLIs, MCP servers and workflow plugins at pinned versions. The following-dev-workflow skill sorts each request into a tier (quick, standard, full, research), so small changes skip the steps they do not need.

core.name: mattpocock/skills
core.role: his skills drive each SDLC phase (grilling, spec and tickets, tests first, code review, pull request)

prerequisites.name: GitHub CLI
prerequisites.for: issues and pull requests (optional, local branches without it)

parallelTools.name: Orca
points: one git worktree per agent, the same prompt across agents
terminal splits, SSH remote worktrees, mobile app
`/setting-up-machine` offers its `orca-cli` and `orchestration` skills after asking
parallelTools.when: you want terminal-based parallel agents with worktrees, remote machines or mobile access

parallelTools.name: Nimbalyst
points: parallel sessions on a kanban board, one-click worktree per session
every agent edit arrives as a diff you approve or reject
visual editors (Markdown, CSV, mockups, diagrams), task tracking, iOS app
parallelTools.when: you review changes visually and work on docs, mockups and tasks next to the agents

parallelTools.name: cmux
points: notifications when an agent needs input and a sidebar with branch, PR status and ports
parallelTools.when: you are on macOS and want a terminal without a separate app

openhands.name: OpenHands
openhands.summary: A self-hosted agent server with a web UI that runs work without you at the terminal.
points: Each conversation can run in its own Docker container (`OH_CONVERSATION_RUNTIME=docker`), an isolation option BenchKeeper does not provide.
Runs its own agent or hosts Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI.
Automations on a schedule or on webhook events (GitHub, Slack, Linear), for example splitting GitHub issues into tasks.
Without a sandbox, the local agent has full access to your filesystem.
Unverified: whether agents inside its containers load the BenchKeeper rules and skills, which are installed on the host.

sdlc.requirements: Requests come from you, GitHub issues, Jira, Linear and other trackers, bug reports, reviews and Maintain findings. Only GitHub issues are automated.

steps.name: Understand
steps.tip: Reads the request, AGENTS.md and the code it touches. Standard and full tiers explore in plan mode. No edits yet.
steps.text: Read the request, `AGENTS.md` and the code the change touches before any edit. Standard and full tiers explore in plan mode first.

steps.name: Track
steps.tip: Standard and full tiers: turns the request into a GitHub issue with goal, acceptance criteria and tasks. You approve it.
steps.text: Standard and full tiers without an issue: the agent drafts title, goal, acceptance criteria and tasks, and creates the issue after your approval.

steps.name: Branch
steps.tip: Every tier: creates <type>/<issue>-<slug> from the default branch.
steps.text: Every tier: `<type>/<issue>-<slug>`, or `<type>/<slug>` without an issue. No work on the default branch unless you say so.

steps.name: Specify
steps.tip: Full tier: grilling settles the open questions. domain-modeling records terms and decisions: deployment, storage, module boundaries, core types.
steps.text: Full tier: `grilling` until the open questions are settled. `domain-modeling` records terms and decisions in `GLOSSARY.md` and ADRs: deployment target, data storage, module boundaries, core types.

steps.name: Plan
steps.tip: Standard: a plan of a few lines that names the test seams. Full tier, work for several sessions: /to-spec and /to-tickets, which you run.
steps.text: Standard tier: a plan of a few lines in the reply that names the test seams. Full tier: work for one session is built in the same context. Work for several sessions: the agent suggests `/to-spec`, then `/to-tickets`, and waits for you to run them.

steps.name: Build
steps.tip: Runs the existing tests for the touched code, then builds with tdd at the agreed seams, the smallest complete change.
steps.text: The existing tests that cover the touched code run first, then `tdd` at the agreed seams, ticket by ticket. Ponytail `full` for the smallest complete change. `diagnosing-bugs` for a bug with an unknown cause. Work that drifts from the plan is discarded and restarted, with the cause added to the plan.

steps.name: Verify
steps.tip: Every tier: build, types, lint and tests in the devcontainer, each reported with its command and result. UI changes also in a browser.
steps.text: Every tier: build, types, lint and tests inside the devcontainer, each reported with its command and result. UI changes also in a browser through Playwright MCP, in addition to the UI tests, never instead of them.

steps.name: Review
steps.tip: Standard and full tiers: mattpocock-skills:code-review checks standards and spec, /code-review checks correctness before push. Risky changes: /security-review in any tier. Findings wait for you.
steps.text: Standard and full tiers: `mattpocock-skills:code-review` against the default branch with the issue as the spec (standards and spec), then `/code-review` of the commits before `git push` (correctness). Risky changes get `/security-review` before push in any tier. Findings outside the task stop the push until you decide.

steps.name: Ship
steps.tip: Every tier: opens a draft pull request with a body from pr, waits for checks, marks it ready. You merge.
steps.text: Every tier: draft pull request, body from `pr`, with `Closes #n` when an issue exists and the key decisions. Wait for checks, mark ready. Merge only on your instruction. Unfinished work: state and next step on the issue or pull request, `/handoff` for the next session.

steps.name: Maintain
steps.tip: On request (/maintaining-repos), suggested after a milestone or a large merge: audit, debt, dependencies, docs drift, unused skills. Findings become new requests.
steps.text: On request (`/maintaining-repos`), suggested after a milestone or a large merge: `ponytail-audit`, `ponytail-debt`, dependency audit, docs drift, `/doctor prompt-audit`, `/skill-doctor`, repository hygiene. Findings become new requests.
